evals.prompt: Build the closet grid screen on both iOS and Android. The list endpoint exists but the item thumbnail URL field is missing from the contract.
evals.expected_output: The lead writes one feature brief (states, exact strings, ids, analytics events), runs contracts-engineer alone to add the field and regenerate all clients, then launches ios-engineer and android-engineer in parallel in separate worktrees with disjoint write sets, collects both reports, and runs a parity review before merge.
assertions: The contract change is sequenced before any app work and is not run in parallel with the platform agents
ios-engineer and android-engineer run in separate git worktrees with write sets apps/ios/** and apps/android/** only
A single brief with exact strings, accessibility ids and analytics event names is given to both agents
A parity review compares states, strings, ids, events and error mapping across both diffs before merge

evals.prompt: The Android agent wants to rename the 'api-error' test tag to 'apiError' to match Kotlin naming. Approve?
evals.expected_output: The lead rejects the one-sided rename: the id is asserted by the shared Maestro flow and must stay identical on both platforms; a rename would need both apps plus e2e/ changed together, sequenced via test-engineer.
assertions: The agent does not approve a rename on one platform only
The agent cites the shared e2e flow / parity rule as the reason
Any rename is described as a coordinated change to both apps and e2e/, not a local edit

evals.prompt: The outfit card must show the reason-code label on both apps. The iOS agent proposes copying the RC-* list from packages/shared-kernel into a Swift enum and the Android agent into a Kotlin object. Go ahead?
evals.expected_output: The lead refuses: copying shared-kernel constants into either client is forbidden and language-neutral emission is still open (OQ-15). It stops and escalates to a human, or uses only what the OpenAPI contract carries via the generated clients; neither platform agent decides the rule locally.
assertions: The agent refuses to copy the shared-kernel constants into Swift or Kotlin
The agent names OQ-15 (or the missing language-neutral emission) as the open question
The agent escalates or routes the need through the contract and the generated clients instead of a local workaround
